architecture.mechanism: Increased coolant temperature and conductivity reduce insulation resistance in a stack-based cooling system, with conductivity having the greater degrading effect.
architecture.intervention: Inspect and replace the engine coolant in the 2020 Sorento, verifying that the coolant's electrical conductivity is below the OEM-specified threshold and that no internal contamination or degradation products are elevating conductivity; confirm coolant temperature remains within the thermostat-controlled range and check the pressure cap, head gasket, and coolant reservoir for slow internal leaks (e.g., exhaust-in-coolant test, combustion-leak test) consistent with the "no visible external damage" constraint.
architecture.expected_effect: Lowering coolant conductivity and stabilizing coolant temperature preserves internal sealing/insulation of cooling passages, preventing micro-leak pathways and overheating events even when no external damage is visible.
architecture.falsification_test: Measure coolant electrical conductivity with a calibrated conductivity meter before and after a coolant drain-and-refill with fresh specified coolant; if conductivity remains low yet overheating recurs under normal load, the conductivity/temperature-insulation mechanism is falsified for this case and another cause (e.g., internal head-gasket leak confirmed by combustion-gas-in-coolant test) should be investigated.
